newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl ready to stand for 1998 election-newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Kohl ready to stand for 1998 election-newspaper.

text.p: Germany's Chancellor Helmut Kohl is prepared to stand in the 1998 general elections for what would be his fourth term as chancellor, the Berliner Morgenpost daily newspaper reported on Friday.
The chancellery was not immediately available for comment on the report that follows weeks of intense speculation over whether Kohl, 63, will stand in general elections next year.
In a report released ahead of publication on Saturday, the newspaper said leaders of junior coalition parties in Kohl's ruling coalition said he had expressed this wish.

The report cited Wolfgang Gerhardt, the chairman of the liberal Free Democrats and Finance Minister Theo Waigel, the leader of the Bavarian-based Christian Social Union, as saying that Kohl had informed each of them personally of his plans.
It also said Kohl, who has come under pressure from his Christian Democrats and the coalition to stand again, would have to convince his family this was the right thing.
This would be particularly hard, it said, because his wife Hannelore was opposed to him standing again.
